ORAL JUDGMENT

In these appeals, the owner of the vehicle is challenging the liability and the petitioners are seeking enhancement of compensation and also questioning the fastening of liability against the owner of the vehicle.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are, on 08.02.2012 at 6.50 p.m., the husband of the first petitioner and father of petitioner Nos.2 to 5, by name Syed Afroz (in short, the 'deceased') while walking on the extreme side of the road at Muvinapur junction, old Guddadahalli, Bengaluru, a Tempo Traveler
bearing

Registration No.KA-02-D-4867 hit NC: 2024:KHC:32987 against the deceased, due to which, he fell down, right side wheel of the Tempo Traveler ran over his stomach, as a result, he succumbed to the injuries on the way to hospital.

He was working as a driver in Parveen Motors,
Bengaluru, earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month plus Rs.100/- bata per day.
The petitioners have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.4,75,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.

Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation and questioning the fastening of liability against the owner of the vehicle, the petitioners are before this Court in M.F.A.No.4305 of 2015.
M.F.A.No.9520 of 2017 has been filed by the owner of the vehicle questioning the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

4. Heard the arguments of Shri M.R.Kumaraswamy, learned counsel for the petitioners, NC:
2024:KHC:32987 Kumari B.R.Roopa, learned counsel appearing on behalf of Shri Anand Beerannavar, learned counsel for owner and Shri H.S.Lingaraju, learned counsel for Insurance Company through video conferencing.
5.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the owner of the vehicle that at the time of accident, the driver was holding valid and effective license to drive the said vehicle.
The Tribunal came to the wrong conclusion that driver did not possess the required driving license and fastened the liability against the owner of the vehicle.
There is no breach of terms and conditions of the policy, hence, the Insurance Company has to indemnify his liability.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the driving license of the deceased is placed before the Tribunal explaining his date of birth as 20.07.1952.
As on the date of accident, the deceased was aged 59 years.
The Tribunal has considered the age of deceased as 60 instead of 59 years erroneously.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32987 deceased was working in Parveen Motors and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month plus Rs.100/- bata per day.
But the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month.
The driver of the tempo traveler was holding a license to drive light motor vehicle, transport, light motor vehicle Cab and PSV Bus.
The tempo traveler is a light motor vehicle.

The principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited 1 is applicable to the facts of this case, but the Tribunal has erroneously fastened the liability against the owner of the vehicle and he has sought for Mrs Mubeena vs Mr Dhanraj J on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22503036/

sentences.text: enhancement of compensation as well as questioned the liability against the Insurance Company.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the post-mortem and inquest report clearly point out that the deceased was aged 60 years.

The Tribunal has rightly considered the age of the deceased; mere production of the driving AIR 2017 SC 3668 NC:
2024:KHC:32987 license of the deceased is not sufficient as the petitioners have not produced any proof of income to show that the deceased was working at Parveen Motors and earning Rs.15,000/-
per month.
The Tribunal has considered the notional income and rightly assessed the compensation.
The compensation assessed is just and proper and it is not a fit case for enhancement.

7.1. It is further contended that the driver of the Tempo Traveler did not possess the valid driving license as there is no endorsement in the driving license to drive the Tempo Traveler, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, Insurance Company can avoid its liability; and the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability against the owner of the vehicle supported the impugned judgment.
8.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for both parties and perused the records.
There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, death of deceased on account of accident.
The petitioners have produced the copy of the driving license pertaining to the deceased marked as Ex.P10 which points out that the date of birth of the deceased is 20.07.1952.
If the date of accident is considered as 08.02.2012, the age of the deceased comes to 59 years.
The Tribunal placed reliance on the post-mortem report, when there is a specific document indicating the date of birth of the deceased, reliance on the post-mortem is not proper.
Hence, age of the deceased has to be taken as 59 years.

The petitioners are the wife and children who are the dependants of the deceased and hence, they are entitled to claim compensation.
10.

The petitioners have produced Ex.P8, Salary Certificate issued by one Parveen Travels in its letter-head wherein it has stated that the deceased was paid Rs.15,000/- salary per month and extra bata paid to the deceased is not mentioned in the said document.
If the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32987 deceased was paid a salary of Rs.15,000/- per month, the income of the deceased is below taxable income and no tax is paid in respect of his employment.
In the letter- head, a salary certificate of this nature cannot be trusted.
Hence, having regard to the accident is of the year 2012, the notional income of the deceased with no proof of income has to be taken as Rs.7,000/- per month.

In a case of this nature, compensation has to be assessed following the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs.- Pranay Sethi and Others2, Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another 3 and Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and Others4.
13.

sentences.text: The petitioners being the five dependants, 1/4 th has to be deducted towards personal expenses whereas for the age of 59 years, future prospects of 10% has to be considered.
In view of judgment in Pranay Sethi's case, since the claim is of the year 2012, 10% appreciation on the conventional heads has to be given.

For the loss of consortium to the wife and loss of love and affection to the children,
Rs.40,000/- each with 10% appreciation comes to Rs.2,20,000/-.
Towards funeral expenses and loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- each has to be assessed.
Thereby, total compensation comes to Rs.8,76,700/- as against Rs.4,75,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, petitioners are entitled for enhancement of (Rs.8,76,700- Rs.4,75,000)=Rs.4,01,700/- which is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
13. As regards the liability is concerned, the Tribunal has not accepted the driving license produced on behalf of the driver of the Tempo Traveler.

Ex.R1 is the copy of the driving license, which points out that the driver of the vehicle was holding a valid license to drive light - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:32987 motor vehicle, transport, light motor vehicle Cab and PSV Bus.

The Tempo Traveler having an unladen weight of 2145 Kgs, the law has been settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan's (supra) case that a person holding a light motor vehicle driving license can also drive the light motor passenger vehicle.
In the light of the said principles, the driving license possessed by the driver of the Tempo Traveler is suffice to drive the said vehicle.
There is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, the liability fastened against the owner of the vehicle is erroneous and the Insurer has to indemnify the Insured.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:

ORDER (i) Both the appeals are allowed in part;
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified;
( v) Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact;

(vi) In view of the cost of Rs.25,000/- being imposed against the owner of the vehicle, the statutory deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal and Insurance Company shall deposit the balance amount.
(vii) Registry is directed to send back the Trial Court Records forthwith.

Sd/-
